title: Dry summers delayed the first autumn records of mushroom-forming fungi in US field observations in 2008-2024, but US herbarium specimens in 1950-2023 showed only a weak, uncertain delay
abstract: Question: a campaign study (sci:2d5ce8d6) found that in nine European countries a dry June-August delayed the 10% date (D10) of July-November records of mushroom-forming fungi (Agaricomycetes) by 7-8 days per 100 mm of water balance. We tested this on a different continent, the contiguous United States, with a pre-registered design. Data: GBIF counts per 5-day bin (no record download) for field observations (all licences, 750,230 records, 2007-2024; and a CC0/CC BY subset) and herbarium specimens (CC0/CC BY, 250,090 records, 1950-2024), with lichen and moss records as an effort reference. Climate: NOAA nClimDiv state and region water balance (precipitation minus Thornthwaite evapotranspiration). Method: unit fixed effects and unit trends, errors clustered by year, joint year permutation, placebo with next-summer water balance. Results: in the seven non-Pacific climate regions a wetter summer made D10 of field observations earlier by 5.2 +/- 2.1 days per 100 mm (38 states, 2009-2024; permutation p < 0.0005) and by 5.5 +/- 1.7 (7 regions). Next-summer water balance and the reference records had no link. The European slope is inside the US interval. 16 of 20 single-state slopes were negative; the Southeast showed no link. In states, heat and drought could not be separated. Herbarium specimens gave only -1.7 +/- 1.4 days per 100 mm (both periods negative, intervals include zero), smaller than the European specimen slope by about 3 standard errors, also on the same region-years. On the Pacific coast, more September-October rain moved D10 and D50 later, opposite to our prediction, because a wet autumn adds late records inside the fixed window. Limitations: record dates are not fruiting dates; 16-17 usable years; coarse state climate; no species composition; all-licence observation counts are not bundled but can be regenerated; pollution was not tested.

Grey band: European observation estimate from sci:2d5ce8d6.
D10 water-balance slopes by NOAA climate region for field observations (states, blue) and herbarium specimens (regions, green). The Pacific regions were not part of the main test.

D10 against June-August water balance after unit effects and unit trends: CC0/CC BY observations (states), specimens (regions) and all-licence observations (ten binned means only). Orange: fitted slope; dashed: European slope.

citations.reason: European result tested here on an independent continent. We use its outcome definitions, record thresholds and effort reference. US field observations support its direction; US specimens do not repeat its specimen slope. No data or code were reused.
